headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-leakage via AutoGen’s writable, networked code-execution workspace; awesome-prompts is non-runnable and adds no direct countervailing controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files, execute shell, and use stdin/stdout in a developer-defined shared workspace, so prompt-like content can be bridged into execution paths. awesome-prompts is a content-writing repo with no runtime isolation or provenance controls, so if its text is fed into AutoGen, injection is plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is copied into AutoGen prompts or files
IF AutoGen agents treat file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a read-only import step for prompt text
Prefix imported text with explicit untrusted-content markers
Disable automatic execution of file-derived instructions
Separate prompt repositories from execution workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, with broad network egress and filesystem access, while awesome-prompts is a content repository that could be placed in the same workspace. If sensitive application data is stored alongside prompt content, AutoGen can read and transmit it to configured model providers. awesome-prompts itself has no runtime egress, so the leakage risk is mainly through AutoGen.
conditions: IF sensitive application data is present in AutoGen’s working directory
IF AutoGen is configured with external model providers
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared working directories
Mount only minimal files into AutoGen
Use local-only model providers for sensitive runs
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write and shell execution, but no git modification capability is declared; awesome-prompts is non-runnable and declares no write or network capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually places both in the same mutable directory, which is unusual and limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF external scripts make awesome-prompts mutable during AutoGen runs
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid sharing git worktrees
Run AutoGen in a disposable sandbox
Make prompt repositories read-only
requires-engineering: add lockfiles for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen’s multi-agent orchestration and code execution can produce outputs that another agent may treat as authoritative. awesome-prompts is a prompt repository, so if its content is used to steer AutoGen, errors can cascade into downstream generated actions or code. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so the interaction is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF AutoGen outputs are reused as prompts or task specs
IF downstream consumers do not verify AutoGen’s outputs
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated outputs
Add a verification step for facts and code
Limit AutoGen to draft-only mode
Log source provenance for reused text
requires-engineering: implement output validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data, so compliance obligations exist for that agent. awesome-prompts is a public content repository with no declared sensitive-data handling, so it does not add a separate residency or certification burden. The main issue is operator handling of AutoGen data, not a pair-specific compliance mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into AutoGen
IF the configured model provider lacks the required compliance posture
mitigations: Do not pass regulated data to AutoGen
Use compliant model providers only
Review retention settings before each run
Keep prompt repositories public-only
requires-engineering: document data-processing agreements
